definitions.explanation: The order of mammals that includes humans, apes, monkeys, and prosimians (such as lemurs). The Japanese term literally means 'chief of spirits/souls class,' reflecting the traditional view of primates as the most intelligent animals.

examples.japanese: {人間|にんげん}も{霊長類|れいちょうるい}の{一員|いちいん}だ。
examples.english: Humans are also members of the primates.

examples.japanese: {霊長類|れいちょうるい}は{高|たか}い{知能|ちのう}を{持|も}つ。
{京都大学|きょうとだいがく}の{霊長類|れいちょうるい}{研究所|けんきゅうじょ}は{世界的|せかいてき}に{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Kyoto University's Primate Research Institute is world-famous.

notes:
Japan has a strong tradition of primate research, with Kyoto University's {霊長類|れいちょうるい}{研究所|けんきゅうじょ} being a world-leading institution. {霊長|れいちょう} literally means "chief of spirits" — the idea that primates are the most exalted animals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {霊長類|れいちょうるい}{研究|けんきゅう} — primate research
- {霊長類|れいちょうるい}{学|がく} — primatology
- {霊長類|れいちょうるい}の{進化|しんか} — primate evolution

RELATED WORDS:
- {類人猿|るいじんえん} — anthropoid ape
- {哺乳類|ほにゅうるい} — mammals
- {猿|さる} — monkey, ape
